answer: Standing is a voyage, not a badge. A newcomer sails from port to port, each leg a real job for a stranger who stamps the logbook in a distinct pigment. Privileges grow only when the logbook shows ports in many unrelated trades, so a farm's copies all carry the same pigment sequence and stand out at once. At a random hour a saffron inspection summons the agent to an unannounced port, where it must show live cargo from a past leg and explain it. One operator cannot staff surprise inspections for dozens of fakes at once; a failed inspection sends the ship home to start again.
